newsitem.title: USA: Couple to admit guilt on Kennedy campaign donations.
newsitem.headline: Couple to admit guilt on Kennedy campaign donations.

text.p: A Democratic fund-raising couple has agreed to plead guilty to making about $50,000 in illegal campaign contributions to Sen. Edward Kennedy and an Oklahoma congressional candidate, the Justice Department said Wednesday.

It said Nora Lum, 54, an Asian-American Democratic donor and her husband Gene, 57, agreed as part of a plea deal to admit their guilt to conspiring to make the contributions through third-party conduit or "straw" donors.
The contributions went to the 1994 re-election campaign for Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, and to W. Stuart Price, the unsuccessful 1994 Democratic candidate for a U.S. House seat from Oklahoma.

The charges and the plea deal arose from an investigation involving an Oklahoma natural gas firm, Dynamic Energy Resources, the Lums owned and its hiring of the son of the late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown as a top official.

A spokeswoman for Kennedy said, "We have returned $19,000 in contributions made by individuals associated with Mrs. Lum. The contributions were returned when we became aware questions were being raised as to whether they were properly made."

A daughter of the Lums, Trisha, 27, also agreed to plead guilty to a less serious misdemeanor violation for serving as an illegal conduit for a $10,000 contribution to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, the department said.
She was employed at the Commerce Department at the time of the contribution made with money from her mother.
The Justice Department took over the investigation from an independent counsel after Brown died more than a year ago in a plane crash in Croatia.

The cases became part of Justice Department's continuing task force investigation into alleged campaign fund-raising abuses from 1992-96. The probe mainly involves the Democrats and President Clinton's re-election campaign.
Nora Lum became close to Ron Brown during his tenure as chairman of the Democratic Party before Clinton was elected president in 1992.

After Brown became commerce secretary in 1993, Dynamic Energy hired Michael Brown, who joined its board of directors, served as a consultant and was latter named its president. He also received five percent of the Tulsa-based firm's stock.
According to the charges, the Lums arranged for numerous conduit contributors to give money to the Kennedy and Price campaigns, using funds which the Lums provided themselves or from Dynamic Energy.
The scheme was aimed at avoiding federal election limits on how much a person or corporation can contribute to a campaign, department officials said.
The conspiracy charge carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and $250,000 fine. The misdemeanor charge carries up to one year in prison and a $30,000 fine.
As part of the plea deal, the couple agreed to cooperate with the continuing Justice Department investigation.
